summary: PNAS 2022 study: the Khufu branch of the Nile and a harbor/canal complex at Giza are well-evidenced; Old Kingdom engineers harnessed the Nile flood to transport materials to the plateau.
content: PNAS 2022 (Sheisha et al.): palaeoecological analysis reconstructs an 8,000-year fluvial history. The Khufu branch of the Nile remained at high water level (~40% of Holocene maximum) during the reigns of Khufu, Khafre, Menkaure, facilitating transport of construction materials. The harbor complex (Ro-She Khufu) is supported by the Wadi el-Jarf papyri, core drillings, and Lehner's model of canals and basins. The fluvial-port-complex hypothesis: builders cut through the western levee and dredged basins to harness the annual 7m flood rise like a hydraulic lift, bringing water to the base of the plateau. This is well-evidenced and strengthens the waterway-transport conclusion.
